Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Health Systems Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during the Q&A, press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Investor Relations Director. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Health Systems' financial results for the third quarter. Joining me on the call are Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Medical Officer; Tom Hargrove, Chief Operating Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Strategy Officer; David Kim, Chief Information Officer; Maria Lopez, Chief Human Resources Officer; and James Whitaker, Chief Compliance Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Michael Reynolds.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the third quarter. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, highlighting areas like our cost reduction efforts, overall financial performance, acuity mix shifts, volume and revenue guidance, value-based care impacts, capital spending plans, revenue per admission dynamics, and supply expense management.

Let's begin with our comprehensive cost reduction initiatives, which have been central to our success. These programs delivered adjusted EBITDA of $285 million for the quarter, a 12% increase year-over-year, while expanding margins to 18.2% from 16.1% last year. Despite flat Medicare inpatient PPS rates at about 2.2% for FY24 and supply chain inflation at 4-6% according to AHA data, we've generated over $220 million in run-rate savings year-to-date, on pace for $300 million annualized by year-end. Across our 42-hospital network, mainly in high-growth Sunbelt areas like Texas, Florida, and the Southeast where bed utilization has rebounded to 68% versus the national 64% per Definitive Healthcare, we've structured this around key pillars.

Labor optimization, our biggest expense at 55% of operating costs, addressed post-pandemic nurse turnover peaking at 27% industry-wide per NSI data, with wage inflation at 7-9%. Our Smart Staffing 2.0 platform, using AI predictive analytics from Cerner and proprietary ML models tied to Epic EHR, cut premium labor like travel nurses and overtime by 42%, from 12% to 7% of nursing payroll, saving $85 million year-to-date. Texas led with 15% reductions thanks to a 20% local RN supply boost from UT Health and Baylor programs. In the Southeast, Florida hospitals reduced scheduling waste by 25% through float pools and cross-training, while prior Northeast divestitures shielded us from New York's 10% wage mandates. We're redirecting 20% of savings, around $17 million, to retention bonuses and training in surging areas like ICU and behavioral health, up 15% year-over-year per MGMA.

On supply chain and procurement, we trimmed 11% off our $1.2 billion annual spend. With med-surg supplies up 5.3% per Vizient's index amid GLP-1 shortages and sterile processing issues, our HealthTrust Purchasing Group role with HCA and Community Health Systems secured 18-22% rebates on ortho implants and cardiac stents. RFID tracking at 15 hospitals dropped stockouts 35% and expired waste 28%, for $42 million saved. Our blockchain vendor portal with McKesson, now in 80% of sites, shortened AP cycles from 45 to 22 days, unlocking $60 million in working capital. Florida localized 40% of pharma amid hurricane risks, beating California peers' 12% hikes. These set us up for 2-3% margin gains in FY25 as steel and resin prices ease.

Back-office and G&A cuts delivered $55 million or 14% off baseline via UiPath RPA in revenue cycle, halving denial rates to 6.5% per HFMA top quartile, lifting cash by $110 million. We consolidated shared services into Dallas, Atlanta, and Tampa hubs, closing five sites and outsourcing coding to Infosys at 25% savings. Telehealth via Zoom-Epic, now 28% of visits, cut overhead 9% with virtual nursing in rural Texas. This ties to value-based care, improving MACRA/MIPS to 92/100 for $18 million CMS ACO savings.

Facility and energy tweaks added $38 million or 8% off utilities via LED retrofits, solar at 22 hospitals with IRA credits, yielding 22% savings—beating Tenet's 7% targets via IoT HVAC. Overall, 450 basis points EBITDA expansion beat Vizient's 150 bps median, capex-neutral at 4.2% of revenue. We've reinvested $50 million in ApexOne precision medicine with Tempus for oncology, strengthening against Medicare Advantage disruptors. Risks like Florida union pushes or 0.3-0.5% CMS IPPS cuts loom, but $100 million more savings in FY26 via gen AI documentation keeps us on 7-9% EBITDA growth track.

Shifting to our key financial performance highlights, we posted consolidated revenue of $2.85 billion, up 9.2% year-over-year and beating consensus by 2%. This is our eighth straight quarter of same-facility growth, with 6.8% patient days increase and 4.5% CMI rise from high-acuity orthopedics, cardio, and oncology. Adjusted EPS hit $1.42, up 12%, with EBITDA at $468 million and 18.9% margins, up 110 basis points.

Inpatient revenue at $1.62 billion, 65% of total, grew 7.9% on 5.2% admissions to 78,400 and 6.8% days to 512,000, plus 4.5% CMI to 1.98, topping HCA and Tenet. Outpatient, 35% mix, surged 14.3% to $862 million on 12.1% encounters to 1.85 million, via 15 freestanding EDs and three ASCs added since Q1 2023 in Texas and Florida.

Payer mix stable: 52% commercial/managed, 32% Medicare, 11% Medicaid, 5% other. RPA up 2.4% to $20,650 from Medicare Advantage and 3.8% Blues hikes. Same-facility revenue +7.6%, organic strength.

EBITDA margin gains from High Reliability Organization and costs: expenses +7.1% to $2.01 billion. Supplies at 28% up 6.2%, offset by $28 million Apex GPO savings. Labor 52%, +8.4% but slowing from Q1 via 15% agency cuts and Talent Pipeline filling 92% RN roles internally; turnover 14.2% vs. 17-20% industry.

Revenue cycle AI from Waystar and Apex Optimizer cut AR days to 42, collections 98.1%, +$52 million EBITDA. Same-facility margins 12.4%, +90 bps over UHS.

Broad-based regionally: Southeast 42% growth on 11% admissions, snowbird demand, JV ASCs. Midwest +8.5% despite Medicaid, via robotics. West +7.2% telehealth +22%. Northeast +5.9% premium mix.

Validates Three Pillars: clinical, digital, inorganic. Epic go-lives at 12 sites, 95% adoption, 25% doc time cut for 15% margin target FY25. Cerner AI patient flow $15-20 million labor savings. Q1 acquisition synergies $12 million, $1 billion pipeline.

Balance sheet: $1.2 billion cash, $2.8 billion liquidity, 2.6x leverage. Capex $185 million 7.5%, ORs/behavioral. $75 million buyback, dividend +8% to $0.42.

Raised FY24 guide: revenue $9.95-10.05 billion +8.5%, EBITDA $1.85-1.90 billion 18.5-19%, EPS $5.65-5.85. Assumes 4-6% admissions, 10-12% outpatient, 4-5% labor inflation. Risks Medicare PFS cuts, supplies, but diversified.

Next, acuity mix changes boosted revenue by 1.8 points of 6.2% net patient revenue growth, or $185 million of $2.1 billion total. Consolidated CMI 1.78, +2.4% YoY, 0.9% sequential. RPA +4.1% to $14,250, acuity 60% of uplift over 2.7% pricing.

Service shifts: high-acuity surgical +7.2%, ortho/cardio; joints +12% DRG 3.2 vs. 1.8 routine, robotics da Vinci Xi at 28 sites. Low-acuity down 4.5% via ASC diversion, 35% ortho/GI outpatient.

Payers: Medicare 52% admissions, FY24 IPPS +5.1%, high-severity DRGs +$92 million, Medicare CMI +3.1%. Commercial 38% +6% bundles like CABG. Medicaid 10% drag offset Texas/Florida.

Sunbelt 62% beds +2.3 CMI, Florida transplants +18% Miami. Midwest/Northeast flat 1.65, countering with $150 million neuro-ICU capex Ohio/PA.

Drivers: CDI with 3M/Nuance +92% queries, +$120 million HCC/SOI. Epic AI acuity forecast staffed high-shift early.

Doubling oncology $300 million Sarah Cannon CAR-T, 340B high-acuity drugs 22% pharmacy. FY24 acuity 1.2-1.5 points growth.

For same-facility volume and revenue guidance, Q3 same-facility revenue +5.2% on 3.1% admissions, 2% RPA. Q4: admissions 2-3.5%, adjusted admissions 3-4.5%, outpatient 5-6.5%; revenue 4.5-6%, RPA $12,500-12,800, CMI +1.5-2.5% offset FY25 IPPS -2.9%.

FY25: admissions 2.5-4%, adjusted 3.5-5%, outpatient 6-7.5%; revenue 5-7%, RPA +2-3.5% to $13,000. CMI 1.88-1.92 neuro/oncology +10%. Lean Six Sigma OR +22%, telehealth 25% follow-ups, VBC 18%.

Regions: Southeast 4.5-6% Florida/Texas 8% ortho; Mid-Atlantic 2.5-4%; West/Midwest 1.5-3.5% ASCs/rural.

Pillars: high-acuity neuro/spine +1,200 beds; site-neutral ASCs 20%; payer 3% hikes. Risks staffing, cyber, economy; $1.2 billion FCF.

Value-based care contracts now 28% net revenue, +6 points YoY from 22%, double Q3 2021. $142 million Q3 reimbursements +17% vs. 4% FFS. MSSP ACOs 15 hospitals 3.2% savings $28 million +25%, readmits 14.8% vs. 15.9% national. Commercial Humana $12 million HCAHPS/opioids.

Net uplift $42 million, RPA +5.2% to $14,200 over 2.8% inflation. Accrued $8 million ortho downside.

Sunbelt 35% VBC, MA 45% +12% capitation knees. Northeast 18%, Medicaid pilots $5 million.

Epic Healthy Planet/Intermountain risk strat -11% ED, -0.8 LOS CHF. AI Lumeris $20 million next year.

To 35% YE24, +10-12% growth, 300 bps margins.

Capital expenditures guided FY24 $425-475 million, 4.8-5.4% of $8.9 billion revenue, +12-22% over 2023 $380 million. Facilities 45% $190-215M: 200 beds Florida/Texas $120M, five ASCs $70M ortho/GI. Equipment 30% $130-140M: Siemens/GE MRI/CT $50M AI workflows, da Vinci $40M. IT 20% $85-95M Epic/Nuance AI $60M, cyber $25M, telehealth +50%. Maintenance 5% $20-25M.

Q1 $115-125M, then $77-100M/quarter. Funds 70% OCF $750M, 20% revolver, 10% equip finance. ROIC 10%+ 2025.

Revenue per admission at $15,420 Q2, +4.7% YoY 1.8% sequential, TTM $15,280 +4.6%. Constant currency +5.2%, 3.1% 5-year CAGR >2.4% Kaufman Hall.

CMI 1.78 +2.3%, cardio DRGs +4.1% TAVR 1,240 +12%, PCI +7%; ortho MS-DRG 522 +9% Mako 15 sites.

Commercial 47% +210 bps, BCBS Texas +5.8%. Medicare 42% MA prune to 18%. Medicaid 11% offset VBC Molina.

Southeast $16,850 +6.2% demo/acuity; Northeast $14,920 +2.9%; West $15,760 +5.4% transplants $285k/case.

LOS 4.62 flat, normalized -2.1% sepsis 94%. Cerner CDI +150 bps CMI, 92% queries +8% capture; Optum coding -22% shifts +$420/admit; R1 $28M denials.

Implants +320 bps Vizient GPO 18% below, $14/admit back. Inflation 2.1% vs. 4.6%.

FY24 +4-4.5%, high-acuity micro-hospitals $250M, Sarah Cannon CAR-T $450k/admit, bundles.

Finally, supply costs $1.247 billion +3.2% YoY, 17.8% revenue -90 bps; other opex $892 million 10.6% -30 bps.

Supplies: med-surg 42% +4.5% 5.8% inflation, Vizient $28M Novaplus IV/cath. Pharma 28% $349M -1.2% 340B 92%, biosimilars 15%, IRA insulin -3%. Implants 22% $274M +5.7% ortho +12%, Medtronic/Stryker bundles 68% $15M, GHX AI -22% stockouts.

Southeast 17.5%, West 18.9% Medi-Cal, Midwest 16.8% 340B. Opex: pro fees $339M +2.1% locums 1.8%, captive docs +14%. Facilities $218M +4.8% energy +6.2%, LED/solar $4.2M IBM -18% downtime. IT $142M +7.5% Epic/Nuance -25% doc, cyber +15%.

Initiatives: RFID/blockchain Cardinal $50M WC; VBC bundles 50% implant share; hubs $35M 2026.

Q3 supplies 17.5-18%, opex 10.5-10.8%, EBITDA 12.8% +110 bps.

Now, I’ll turn the call over to Lisa Chen to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Michael. Good morning, everyone. As Michael outlined, we had an exceptionally strong quarter. Net revenue for the third quarter was $2.85 billion, an increase of 9.2% compared to the same period last year. This growth stemmed from higher patient volumes, better acuity and payer mix, revenue cycle gains, and acquisition contributions.

Our operating expenses were $2.39 billion, representing 84% of net revenue. We're tightly controlling costs while investing in growth, especially labor and supplies.

Net income for the quarter was $285 million, or $1.85 per share. We're raising full-year guidance across the board.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Raj Patel for an update on our clinical initiatives.

Dr. Raj Patel:
Thank you, Lisa. Good morning. We're advancing clinical outcomes and satisfaction markedly. Our Heart Failure Management Program delivered a 20% reduction in readmission rates. We're harnessing telehealth, remote monitoring, and AI diagnostics to elevate patient experience and coordination.

Following that, Tom Hargrove will update on operations.

Tom Hargrove:
Thank you, Dr. Patel. We're streamlining across our network with Lean Six Sigma for patient flow and centralized supply chain management, yielding major savings, smoother throughput, and higher staff output.

Next, Elena Vasquez on strategy.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Tom. We're prioritizing network growth, partnerships, and tech innovation, pursuing expansions in prime markets, new services, and revenue diversification.

After that, David Kim on IT and cybersecurity.

David Kim:
Thank you, Elena. Our IT is robust and secure for operations and data protection. New measures strengthen cybersecurity, ensure regs compliance, and counter breaches. Cloud solutions boost scalability.

Following that, Maria Lopez on workforce.

Maria Lopez:
Thank you, David. We're attracting and retaining top talent with satisfaction programs, training, and diversity culture.

Finally, James Whitaker on compliance.

James Whitaker:
Thank you, Maria. We're upholding top ethics and compliance via a full program safeguarding privacy and curbing fraud.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to Michael Reynolds.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, everyone. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Our first question comes from Alex Rivera with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good morning. Can you provide more details on the specific initiatives you are implementing to improve employee satisfaction and retention?

Maria Lopez:
Good morning, Alex. Absolutely. We're rolling out comprehensive retention strategies, including competitive bonuses tied to performance in high-demand areas like ICU, with $17 million allocated from labor savings. Our Talent Pipeline program has filled 92% of RN openings internally, dropping turnover to 14.2% from 18.5%. Upskilling via cross-training and partnerships with local universities like UT Health boosts engagement, while diversity initiatives and float pools cut inefficiencies by 25%. Employee surveys show satisfaction up 15%, and we're piloting mental health support post-pandemic.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Jordan Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Jordan Lee:
What are your plans for addressing the ongoing challenges related to regulatory compliance and cybersecurity threats?

James Whitaker:
Thanks, Jordan. Our compliance program is enterprise-wide, with rigorous HIPAA and fraud prevention training across all 42 facilities. Post-Change Healthcare, we've invested $25 million in zero-trust architecture and HHS-aligned cyber enhancements, reducing breach risks significantly. Regular audits and AI monitoring for anomalies ensure MIPS scores at 92/100, unlocking ACO savings. We're also proactive on 340B scrutiny and IPPS rules.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Taylor Brooks with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Taylor Brooks:
Can you elaborate on the potential impact of your strategic acquisitions on your long-term growth prospects?

Elena Vasquez:
Hi, Taylor. Our recent Southeast tuck-ins are tracking $12 million synergies, with a $1 billion pipeline in ambulatory assets mirroring HCA's model. These add high-acuity capacity and ASCs, boosting same-facility growth to 5-7% FY25. They diversify payer mix, enhance VBC penetration to 35%, and position us for 10% CMI lift in oncology/neuro, driving sustained EBITDA expansion.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Chris Patel with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Chris Patel:
How are you leveraging AI to improve diagnostic accuracy?

Dr. Raj Patel:
Good morning, Chris. AI is transformative—our Epic-integrated predictive tools forecast acuity shifts 15% ahead, optimizing staffing. Nuance CDE and 3M CDI capture 92% queries for precise HCC/SOI documentation, adding $120 million revenue. In diagnostics, Siemens/GE AI workflows cut MRI/CT times 20-30%, boosting throughput. Oncology AI with Tempus in ApexOne enhances precision therapies, reducing errors and readmits by 20% in heart failure.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sam Wong with Wells Fargo. Please go ahead.

Sam Wong:
Can you expand on FY25 capex priorities?

Lisa Chen:
Sure, Sam. FY25 capex holds at $425-475 million, focused 45% on capacity like 200 beds and ASCs, 30% equipment for robotics/MRI, 20% IT for Epic AI and cyber. This supports 3.5-5% adjusted admissions growth, with quick ROI from efficiencies like 22% OR turnover.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the Apex Health Systems Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
